questions.question_text: For which values of $x$ is $y=\ln(\ln x)$ defined, and what is its derivative?

options.why: Required only $x>0$ for the inside $\ln x$, but the outer logarithm also needs $\ln x>0$.
Used $\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$ and left out the inner derivative $f'(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}$.
Wrote the reciprocal of the correct derivative, inverting the fraction.

questions.solution_text:
$\ln(\ln x)$ needs $\ln x>0$, so $x>1$.
$f(x)=\ln x$, so $f'(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{x}}{\ln x}$
$=\dfrac{1}{x\ln x}$
